title: Grade 8 Science — Fri, Jun 13
description: Metals and Non-metals — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — property identification, reactions, non-metals
subject: science

questions.question: Which of the following properties belongs to NON-metals?
options: Poor conductors of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity. They are brittle, not malleable or ductile, and lack metallic lustre.

questions.question: Which property do ALL metals share?
options: They are all solid at room temperature
They are all good conductors of electricity
They all have high melting points
They all react with cold water
questions.explanation: All metals are good conductors of electricity (mercury is a liquid but still conducts). Mercury is the exception to 'all solid'.

questions.question: A student observes that a substance conducts electricity and can be hammered into a sheet. This substance is most likely:
questions.explanation: Electrical conductivity and malleability (hammering into sheets) are characteristic properties of metals.

questions.question: Carbon exists in multiple forms. Which form of carbon can conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite has a layered structure with free electrons between layers, making it a good conductor — unlike diamond or coal.

questions.question: Predict: Will zinc displace copper from copper sulphate solution? Why?
options: No, because zinc is less reactive than copper
Yes, because zinc is more reactive than copper and can displace it
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the reactivity series, so it displaces copper: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.

questions.question: Which non-metal is essential for life and makes up about 21% of air?
questions.explanation: Oxygen (O₂) makes up ~21% of air and is essential for respiration in all aerobic organisms.

questions.question: The non-metal element used in pencil leads is:
questions.explanation: Pencil 'leads' contain graphite (a form of carbon) mixed with clay. The word 'lead pencil' is a historical misnomer.

questions.question: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) released by burning coal and volcanic eruptions causes:
questions.explanation: SO₂ reacts with rainwater to form sulphurous and sulphuric acid, causing acid rain which damages forests and buildings.

questions.question: A metal X reacts vigorously with cold water but not with dilute acid (it's too reactive and causes explosion). Metal X is likely:
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium are so reactive they react explosively with water and are kept under oil to prevent contact with air and moisture.

questions.question: Iron + sulphur → iron sulphide (FeS). This is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Combination (synthesis) reaction: two substances combine to form one new compound. Fe + S → FeS.

questions.question: Which metal is used in making electrical wires due to its high ductility and good conductivity?
questions.explanation: Copper has excellent electrical conductivity and high ductility (can be drawn into thin wires). It is the most common electrical conductor.

questions.question: The non-metal chlorine reacts with metals to form:
questions.explanation: Chlorine (Cl₂) reacts with most metals to form metal chlorides. E.g., 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl (sodium chloride — table salt).

questions.question: Which statement about mercury is CORRECT?
options: Mercury is a solid non-metal at room temperature
Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature
Mercury does not react with other chemicals
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature (melting point -39°C). It is highly toxic.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct comparison between metals and non-metals?
options: Both are good conductors of electricity
Metals are malleable; non-metals are brittle
Non-metals have metallic lustre; metals do not
questions.explanation: Metals are malleable (can be hammered). Non-metals are brittle (break when hit). This is a key differentiating property.

questions.question: Phosphorus is stored under water because it:
options: Needs water to maintain its colour
Ignites spontaneously in air (highly reactive with oxygen)
Floats on water when stored in air
questions.explanation: White phosphorus is extremely reactive — it spontaneously ignites in air. Storing it under water prevents contact with oxygen.
